recipes.name: Panzanella Salad
ingredients_raw: 6 cups day old Italian bread, torn into bite-size pieces
4 medium ripe tomatoes, cut into wedges
0.5 cup pitted and halved green olives
1 cup fresh mozzarella, cut into bite-size pieces

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Toss bread with 1/3 cup olive oil, salt, pepper, and garlic in a large bowl.
Arrange on a baking sheet and toast in the preheated oven until golden, about 5 to 10 minutes.
Transfer bread back into the bowl and set aside to cool slightly.
Whisk 1/4 cup of olive oil and balsamic vinegar together in a small bowl; set aside.
Add tomatoes, onion, basil, olives, and mozzarella into the bowl with bread; toss with vinaigrette.
Let stand for 20 minutes before serving. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Panzanella Salad
raw_recipe.description: Panzanella is an Italian salad made with toasted bread cubes, ripe tomatoes, and basil, tossed with a simple vinaigrette for a delicious summer salad.

video.description: Fresh mozzarella, vinaigrette, olives or capers, make an excellent Greek Salad. Homemade croutons and basil add a taste of comfort and while the red onions give a nice crunch and spiciness. Serve with your favorite pasta dish or take with you to a potluck!

review.reviewBody: In my opinon, your ingredient choices will make or break this salad from 5 star plus to a 2 or 3 star. I have had this about 6 or 7 times (various recipes). By FAR the best is using stale hard rolls or very-chewy Italian bread. If you don't, the bread just becomes mushy instead of that wonderful, chewy, garlic-bread bites that is so special in this recipe. Alot of the flavor is from your choice garlic and oil, too. I use a high quality EVOO and FRESH only: minced garlic, mozzarella and basil leaves. If you don't use the fresh, it alters the flavor significantly. I think cherry or grape tomato's texture is better suited for this. Capers are a nice added flavor and, as I discovered tonight, so is roasted asparagas. With all that being said...made with our preferences, this goes in the favorite file.
Excellent summer salad. I used Kalamata olives in place of the green (b/c that's what I had.) Everyone raved about this dish! Can't wait to try w/ capers! Thanks for the recipe!

What a nice twist to the traditional recipe. I loved the idea of toasting the bread with the garlic, oil and seasonings (I used an herb blend). It mellowed the garlic just enough to take the edge off. I left the salt out of the recipe and added brined capers to compensate. I suggest that the mozzarella cubes be added after the salad is plated to preserve their deliciousness. By the way, I used a chewy bread for this recipe - ciabatta was what I had and it really held up. I'm sure focaccia would work such as well. Don't waste your time with supermarket breads for this tasty dish. Thanks for a great recipe!

I just made this last night and today it's the featured recipe! I used 1 container of fresh bocconcini from Trader Joe's and subbed a handful of capers for the green olives. Also added 1/2 an English cucumber, chopped, and let the veggies (minus the basil which I added at the end) marinate in the vinegar and oil while I toasted the bread in the oven. Then rubbed the bread with the raw garlic - sooo delicious!! Also, I served this immediately so the bread still had some crunch.

I think it is better to bake the bread pieces at a low temperature for a longer time. This will harden the bread and keep it from becoming mushy. Sorry, I use Olive Garden dressing or balsamic on everything. I would like to add balsamic roasted veggies to this though i.e. onions, bell peppers, small tomatoes and asparagus. Use Castelvetrano olives if you don't care for regular olives. They are mild and have less salt. You have to pit them though. Otherwise Kalamata, Greek or oil cured olives are great for Panzanella.

This was really fabulous! A few notes:

It makes way more than you think...seriously, my 4 QUART bowl was overflowing - adjust accordingly.

I used ciabatta bread and it was perfect. Even after sitting in the fridge for a few days, the bread was no longer crunchy but it wasn't slimy or mushy as bread can get. Definitely add the garlic while you toast the bread - it gives it a fantastic flavor.

As recommended by others I added half a bag of baby spinach, cut into strips, as well as some artichoke hearts. 

The overall result was wonderful. I'll be making this again and again!

OMG this is super good! I used white balsamic vinegar, no onions, because they are too overpowering, and no olives, personal choice. The flavors mix wonderfully and it's the perfect summer salad. It was so hot here today that I toasted the bread on the bbq in a pan of course, using the indirect method, they came out perfect and had that smokey flavor. I used smart balance instead of olive oil on the bread too. I will make this again and again! Thanks for a great recipe!

Omitted the onion, subbed black olives for green, and halved grape tomatoes instead or regular cubed, and used a little more olive oil as needed to fry the bread cubes in a deep skillet to retain crunch after dressing was applied. More basil also to use up what came in the package. Very good with roasted chicken for Mothers' Day.

Easy and delicious! I brought this to my friend’s house as a side dish to her luncheon. I oven toasted the bread, and prepped all other ingredients in advance. Thanks to another reviewers note, I put all non bread ingredients in a glass serving bowl, put the oven toasted bread on top, and refrigerated it until I had to leave (about 2-2.5 hours). Right before leaving I tossed all ingredients, and added the olive oil/balsamic vinegar dressing (tossing again to mix). The flavors blended during my 40-45 minute drive, which my nose was very happy about ;-). The salad was a huge hit! I LOVE allrecipes almost as much as I love the help I get from the other reviewers :-). P.S. I followed the recipe to a ‘t’ except for using cherry tomatoes instead of regular sized tomatoes. The bread I used was the fat ‘chewy’ french style bread baked fresh at Costco.
I love this salad. Very light and refreshing. Took it to a cookout and came home with no leftovers. I left the croutons out until the day of the event. They would of ended up too soggy.

I have made this twice, and it was a hit both times. I also added cucumbers and omitted the seeds, red and yellow peppers, celery, and shallots. I added both green and Kalamata olives. You need to let the bread soak in the olive oil while you are making the rest of the salad. I did not do that the first time, and I felt the bread was too hard. Thank you for a great recipe
I made the recipe exactly as described, and added fresh avocado. The great thing about this recipe is you can add so many things things. This is definitely a keeper!
Few simple ingredients to make an easy and filling salad. Will be making this often this summer!
I didn't toast the bread cubes and still delicious. Will toast next time.
This is so delicious! The only thing I would do different next time is cut back on the onions. Thanks for sharing!
So easy! I added more spice to give it a kick but it was an awesome base!
Delicious! Subbed out the olives for capers to appease the hubs.
Now it is my favorite salad!
Family LOVES this salad!

This was amazingly delicious. Made this for lunch the day before Thanksgiving to accompany soup- wanted something other than a traditional salad and this was perfect. Everyone loved it and no leftovers. I did use halved cherry tomatoes instead of chopped tomatoes and used Kalamata olives instead of green olives. I also added some capers and artichoke hearts . I would definitely make again.
